newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: BOTSWANA STOCKS WEEK - DOMESTIC MARKET ON THE RISE.
newsitem.headline: BOTSWANA STOCKS WEEK - DOMESTIC MARKET ON THE RISE.

text.p: The domestic market continued its
upward trend with the index adding 3.26 points to close at
442.75 for the week on Friday.
A large block of milling company and food wholesaler
Sefalana shares were traded at 430 thebe and 440 thebe.
The stock closed 10 thebe up at 440.
Volumes were otherwise low. Botswana Insurance
traded at 220 thebe and is now bid up at 225 thebe. A small
block of First National traded at 550 thebe, unchanged
on the week.
Security group Inco slipped five thebe to 90. Food
and tobacco wholesaler Metsef increased its trade by
five thebe to reach 650. Brewery holding company
Sechaba traded at 320 thebe and closed at 325 thebe.
Untraded were Barclays 725/750 thebe, oil company
Engen 445/475 thebe, investment company Kgola ya
Sechaba 180/190 thebe, clothing chain Pep at 300
thebe with buyers only, variable loan stock company RDC
Properties at 170 thebe, and Standard
Chartered bid up five thebe to end at 625.
Overall turnover was up with 864,745 domestic shares
exchanging hands compared to a previous 363,180, valued at
3,780,322 pula over an earlier 1,015,062 pula.
There was no trade on the foreign dual-listed board. Car
rental and fleet management group Avis put on 38 thebe
to close at 640, De Beers dropped to 12,754 thebe from
12,819, McCarthy Retail group ended at 1,135 thebe from
1,143 and Regent Undervalued Assets Africa Fund was
unchanged at 4,000 thebe.
The index closed 1.60 points down at 392.50 and the Overall
Index shed 1.48 points to close at 393.80.
